title: files: an authorization gap in the file lifecycle after a file is released, within one organization (detail withheld)
body:
**Filing gate ①, the "may leak data" exception, on the maintainer's direct word.** Found by the design review of PR #25971 (the ADR-0104 D3 amendment for #25692), and first noted by the #25692 dev. Filed by the `domain:server` seat 2 thread (seat post #20966, session `session_01TFnDdepdwyDJeM2kJ4GtMy`). ⛔ Not a claim. Domain, grade and route are triage's.

**The maintainer's words**, choosing on that review: 「先改措辞,再批,另开两张卡」 (2026-10-26, decision card in the seat thread). This is the second of the two cards.

**Disclosure:** the mechanism and the path are withheld from every public surface under the security-family discipline, as on #25692. The seat thread holds them and has handed them to the maintainer; the dev who takes this card gets them from whoever dispatches it, through the maintainer's project.

**What can be said:** the gap sits in the file-reference lifecycle (ADR-0104 D3, `packages/services/service-storage`), within one organization, on the path a file takes after its owning record lets it go. It predates PR #25951, which did not widen it. ADR-0104 promises one file, one owning record and one access rule; at that point in the file's life the rule is weaker than the record's.

**Business reason:** any deployment whose private records hold files (contracts, IDs, HR attachments) relies on that one access rule holding for every member of the organization, including after a file is replaced or removed from its record. Not fixing it leaves a window in which the rule does not hold.

**Reader who acts:** after triage, the `domain:server` lane (`packages/services/service-storage`, the file-reference lifecycle). The fix needs a line in ADR-0104 D3, which is the maintainer's. ⛔ The public ADR text does not describe the gap before the fix lands.

**Dedupe:** the nearest cards are #25692 (closed by PR #25951), #25693, #25694 and #25704. None of them covers this path. **New.**
